dormant_note: Step change and Volatile need at least 10 readings to mean anything and a 4 day window does not give that, so they stay quiet on a weekly run. Flatline always looks back 14 days regardless, because on a week a genuinely steady site is indistinguishable from one that is not measuring.

mapal_gap_note: Mapal currently only flags chicken below 4.0 and tonkotsu below 6.0, and flags nothing high. So it misses every chicken reading between 4.0 and 5.0, and every reading above 7.0, both of which are out of spec.

resolution.note: Most of the estate only ever records whole numbers. A refractometer reads to one decimal, so a whole number is a rounded number. On a window only 1.0 or 2.0 wide, rounding to the nearest whole unit is a big fraction of the tolerance and it hides small drifts entirely. Sites already reporting decimals prove the meters can do it.

cases.headline: Consistently too strong
cases.response: Method check at the pass. Watch one batch made start to finish: what vessel is the water measured with, and is the ratio the current spec? Too strong almost always means under-watering a concentrate. Re-read with the chef present and agree the ratio in writing before you leave.

cases.headline: Not measuring
cases.response: Unannounced visit. Watch the check being taken, then take it yourself on the same pot and compare. If the refractometer is missing, broken or uncalibrated, replace it before anything else. Do not treat this as a broth problem until a real reading exists.
cases.evidence: one DEC-witnessed reading, plus 5 consecutive days of varying readings after
cases.owner: Penny (DEC Scotland & Newcastle)

cases.headline: Sitting on the bottom edge
cases.response: Technically inside 4.0 to 5.0 but parked against the bottom of it and well away from where the rest of the estate sits. There is no margin left, so one ordinary bad day puts it out. Check the ratio and move it toward the middle of the window rather than waiting for it to fail.
cases.owner: Artur Mroczkowski (DEC North England & Midlands)

estate_actions.title: Set the Mapal comparer to the real windows
estate_actions.why: Mapal catches 1 of 32 out-of-spec readings and misses 31. It has no upper limit configured at all, and over-strength is now essentially the whole problem.
estate_actions.do: Change the Chicken Broth Check comparer to 4.0-5.0 and the Tonkotsu Broth Check to 6.0-7.0. Every one of those misses then raises itself as a deviation at the point of failure, on the chef's screen, with a corrective action required.
estate_actions.effect: turns this whole page from a fortnightly report into a live control

estate_actions.title: Require one decimal place on both broth checks
estate_actions.why: 21 of 38 site lines (55.3%) only ever record whole numbers, on windows just 1.0 wide. A site writing 5 on a 4 to 5 chicken window is sitting exactly on the ceiling, and small drifts are invisible.
estate_actions.do: Set the answer option to one decimal, and say so in the task text.
estate_actions.effect: makes the window usable and the drift detectable

estate_actions.title: Set a factory target band
estate_actions.why: The factory has no spec, so it can only be scored on steadiness. It could slide from 8.30 to 7.60 over a month, smoothly, and keep scoring in the 90s.
estate_actions.do: Give a min and max for factory tonkotsu and chicken after ice.
estate_actions.effect: the factory panel scores against a target instead of just measuring steadiness
